title: MCP document server + filesystem pin + recovery
acceptance_criterion: Tools work through the protocol and a repeated action does not duplicate the mock effect
verdict: The 'no duplicate effect' half of the AC is solidly met (idempotent ledger). The 'tools work through the protocol' half is met only in-process for 2 tools and is not exercised end to end or wired into any run. NOT complete.
evidence: src/agentops_workbench/mcp/mcp_servers/document/server.py: stdio JSON-RPC handler — initialize / tools/list / tools/call for search_docs + read_document; unknown tool -> -32601
tests/mcp/test_document_server.py = 22 tests pass: handshake, error classification (timeout/disconnect/malformed/...), scope refusal, client-reinit-after-disconnect
tests/mcp/test_document_server.py::test_duplicate_publish_is_idempotent — re-publish with same action_key does not duplicate; different args -> DuplicateArgsError
gaps: The document server exposes 2 tools (search_docs, read_document), not the 5 the EVIDENCE_CARD claims. get_issue exists only as a prompt string; create_ticket_draft / publish_ticket are not MCP tools (only TicketLedger.publish()).
No agent run invokes the MCP server: the fixed graph reads fixtures/docs directly; single_agent / planner_executor have '# Tool dispatch is a stub for MVP' and never call it.

'Tools work through the protocol' is verified only at the in-process handle_request level; main_stdio is '# pragma: no cover' and there is no test that spawns the server as a subprocess and drives it over stdio.
The pinned @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem is represented by an in-repo FilesystemGuard + InMemoryDocumentClient; the real npm server is not launched in any test.

synthesized.note: The /dev-kit:build runner was never executed in this monorepo. The AgentOps Workbench was built in a standalone repo and imported via PR #8, so no per-step sub-agent subprocess output was ever captured. This file is an audit of the shipped tree under apps/agentops-workbench/ against the step's acceptance criterion, plus a re-run of the deterministic gates on 2026-09-11. status / acceptance_met are judgements against the code as merged, not a recorded process exit.
